universe.name: Universe
universe.description: A bounded demonstration catalog of the Solar System, confirmed exoplanets and twenty named galaxies. The spatial layout and procedural appearances are illustrations, not a measured three-dimensional model.

galaxies.name: Milky Way
galaxies.description: The Milky Way is the galaxy containing the Solar System. This demonstration includes a bounded selection of its confirmed nearby planetary systems.

clouds.name: Solar Neighborhood
clouds.description: This local navigation region contains the Solar System and 15 additional confirmed planetary systems at archive-reported distances within 15 parsecs. It is a bounded selection of nearby hosts, not a complete census or a claim of shared physical interstellar-cloud membership. Other regions retain their IAU sky-constellation groupings.

systems.name: Solar System
systems.description: The Solar System contains the Sun and eight planets. Planet sizes, distances, surfaces and orbital motion in this map are illustrative.

star.name: Sun
star.description: The Sun is the star at the center of the Solar System. NASA lists its effective temperature as 5772 kelvin and its mean radius as 695700 kilometers.

planets.name: Mercury
planets.description: Mercury is the smallest planet in the Solar System and the closest planet to the Sun.

planets.name: Venus
planets.description: Venus is the second planet from the Sun. Its dense atmosphere traps heat, making it the hottest planet in the Solar System.

planets.name: Earth
planets.description: Earth is the third planet from the Sun and the only world currently known to support life.

planets.name: Mars
planets.description: Mars is the fourth planet from the Sun. Iron minerals in its surface material give it a reddish appearance.

planets.name: Jupiter
planets.description: Jupiter is the largest planet in the Solar System. It is a gas giant, made mostly of hydrogen and helium.

planets.name: Saturn
planets.description: Saturn is a gas giant surrounded by prominent rings composed mostly of pieces of ice.

planets.name: Uranus
planets.description: Uranus is an ice giant with a rotation axis tilted by about 98 degrees. It is the seventh planet from the Sun.

planets.name: Neptune
planets.description: Neptune is an ice giant and the eighth planet from the Sun. It is the most distant of the eight Solar System planets.

galaxies.name: Andromeda
galaxies.description: Andromeda, also called Messier 31, is a large spiral galaxy in the Local Group. This demonstration does not place confirmed exoplanets in this galaxy.

galaxies.name: Triangulum
galaxies.description: Triangulum, also called Messier 33, is a spiral galaxy in the Local Group. No planetary systems are included here in this demonstration.

galaxies.name: Whirlpool
galaxies.description: Whirlpool, also called Messier 51, is a spiral galaxy whose prominent arms contain star-forming regions. No planetary systems are included here in this demonstration.

galaxies.name: Pinwheel
galaxies.description: Pinwheel, also called Messier 101, is a face-on spiral galaxy. No planetary systems are included here in this demonstration.

galaxies.name: Bode's Galaxy
galaxies.description: Bode's Galaxy, also known as Messier 81, is a spiral galaxy in Ursa Major. Its spiral arms contain populations of young, blue stars. No planetary systems are included here in this demonstration.

galaxies.name: Black Eye
galaxies.description: Black Eye, also known as Messier 64, is a spiral galaxy in Coma Berenices. A prominent band of dust partly obscures its bright central region. No planetary systems are included here in this demonstration.

galaxies.name: Sunflower
galaxies.description: Sunflower, also known as Messier 63, is a flocculent spiral galaxy in Canes Venatici. Its patchy arms are less sharply defined than those of a grand-design spiral. No planetary systems are included here in this demonstration.

galaxies.name: Southern Pinwheel
galaxies.description: Southern Pinwheel, also known as Messier 83, is a spiral galaxy in Hydra. Its dusty spiral arms contain many young star clusters. No planetary systems are included here in this demonstration.

galaxies.name: Messier 95
galaxies.description: Messier 95, also called NGC 3351, is a barred spiral galaxy in Leo. It belongs to the Leo I or M96 galaxy group. No planetary systems are included here in this demonstration.

galaxies.name: Messier 96
galaxies.description: Messier 96, also called NGC 3368, is a spiral galaxy in Leo. Its asymmetric arms and off-center core are influenced by interactions with neighboring galaxies. No planetary systems are included here in this demonstration.

galaxies.name: Messier 98
galaxies.description: Messier 98 is a spiral galaxy in the Virgo Cluster, seen in the direction of Coma Berenices. Its gas and dust support numerous star-forming regions. No planetary systems are included here in this demonstration.

galaxies.name: Messier 99
galaxies.description: Messier 99 is a grand-design spiral galaxy in Coma Berenices. Its long, clearly defined spiral arms contain stars and star-forming material. No planetary systems are included here in this demonstration.

galaxies.name: Messier 100
galaxies.description: Messier 100 is a grand-design spiral galaxy in the Virgo Cluster. Its prominent, dusty arms contain regions of active star formation. No planetary systems are included here in this demonstration.

galaxies.name: Sculptor
galaxies.description: Sculptor, also called NGC 253 or Caldwell 65, is a spiral galaxy viewed nearly edge-on. Intense star formation earns it a starburst classification. No planetary systems are included here in this demonstration.

galaxies.name: NGC 1300
galaxies.description: NGC 1300 is a barred spiral galaxy in Eridanus. Its main spiral arms extend from the ends of a straight central bar of stars. No planetary systems are included here in this demonstration.

galaxies.name: NGC 1365
galaxies.description: NGC 1365 is a barred spiral galaxy in Fornax and a member of the Fornax Cluster. Its large central bar connects to two prominent spiral arms. No planetary systems are included here in this demonstration.

galaxies.name: NGC 2403
galaxies.description: NGC 2403, also called Caldwell 7, is a spiral galaxy in Camelopardalis. Its ionized hydrogen clouds are active sites of star formation. No planetary systems are included here in this demonstration.

galaxies.name: NGC 2903
galaxies.description: NGC 2903 is a barred spiral galaxy in Leo. Dust lanes and young star clusters trace its arms and the region around its central bar. No planetary systems are included here in this demonstration.

galaxies.name: Fireworks
galaxies.description: Fireworks, also called NGC 6946, is an intermediate spiral galaxy with a high rate of star formation. Frequent observed supernovae gave the galaxy its nickname. No planetary systems are included here in this demonstration.

provenance.source: NASA Exoplanet Archive / Planetary Systems Composite Parameters
provenance.query: select pl_name,hostname,pl_letter,pl_controv_flag,sy_snum,sy_pnum,cb_flag,sy_dist,ra,dec,disc_year,discoverymethod,pl_orbper,pl_orbperlim,pl_orbper_reflink,st_spectype,st_teff,st_tefflim,st_teff_reflink,st_rad,st_radlim,st_rad_reflink,st_age,st_agelim,st_age_reflink,sy_dist_reflink,disc_refname from pscomppars where pl_controv_flag=0 and sy_snum=1 and cb_flag=0 and hostname in (select hostname from pscomppars where sy_dist<=100 and ra is not null and dec is not null) order by hostname,pl_name
provenance.constellationMethod: Astropy get_constellation: ICRS coordinates precessed to B1875; Roman 1987 IAU boundaries
provenance.selection: Single-star, non-circumbinary confirmed planets with no published confirmation controversy; complete eligible host groups selected from a 100 pc source pool. Priority nearby hosts precede planet-rich hosts; the 31 highest-ranked real constellation regions are retained. Fifteen additional eligible nearby hosts are added to Solar Neighborhood without moving any existing constellation system. This is a bounded demonstration, not a full nearby census.

nearbySelection.selectionNote: Additional single-star confirmed-planet hosts, ordered by their archive-reported distance, are selected from the pinned source pool only when absent from the existing constellation cohort. Complete eligible host groups are added after the Solar System without moving or replacing any existing system, planet or parent. This nearby selection is intentionally incomplete.

provenance.descriptions: Planet descriptions use source names, host relationships, discovery year/method and only positive orbital periods with a zero limit flag. Missing facts are omitted. No climate, surface, habitability or life claim is inferred for an exoplanet.
provenance.stellarParameters: Optional non-limited stellar temperature, radius and age are copied from a source row; stellar radius in Solar radii is multiplied by NASA's 695700 km nominal Solar radius. Composite fields can have different literature references, retained in the raw snapshot. Stellar age estimates above the approximately 13.8-billion-year age of the universe are omitted from display because this interface does not show their uncertainties; the raw NASA snapshot is unchanged.
provenance.appearance: Visual seeds preserve deterministic illustrations. Positions, colors, surfaces, rings, sizes, spacing and motion are not observed exoplanet measurements.
provenance.attribution: NASA Exoplanet Archive, operated by Caltech under contract with NASA's Exoplanet Exploration Program; individual parameter references are retained in the raw snapshot.
